content.thinking:
I need to carefully plan out the whole model in one pass without testing, so I want to design a phoenix standing with wings spread on a small base, working out proportions like body height, leg placement, and head position to keep everything proportioned and grounded at y=0.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy: a hips root joint, then a spine chain running up to the chest, followed by a neck chain curving forward into the head, making sure each chain's parent and path points connect smoothly without gaps.

Still shaping the body path...

I'm planning the body's coloring with a cel-shaded gradient running from deep crimson at the top down through orange to a gold belly.

Now I'm defining the color palette: crimson, orange, gold, pale yellow, a deep plum shadow tone, and a teal accent, then sketching how cel-shading with countershading will apply to the body coat. For the wings, I'm planning feather and flame-tongue textures as SVG cards, with each wing built as a skeletal chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist leading into the primary feathers.

Writing wing joint coordinates...

I'll give each feather a slight bend to curl downward, and attach each card row to a specific bone (wrist, forearm, upper arm) rather than letting it auto-detect. Now I'm mapping out the actual feather layout per wing: primaries fanning from the hand, secondaries along the forearm pointing back, coverts as smaller rows near the leading edge, and tertials from the upper arm, with enough density to read as a solid wing surface.

I'm scaling this down a bit since a 4.4m wingspan feels too large for the body—dropping primaries to 0.85m for roughly a 3.9m span, which still feels dramatically eagle-like without being absurd. I also need to make sure nothing dips below the floor: feet rest at y=0, and while tail feathers can trail low, I'll keep most above 0.05 except a couple of drooping ones near 0.02. For the legs, I'm working out hip-to-foot positions and segment lengths (thigh, shin, tarsus) to match the actual limb distance.

Now I'm defining the leg joint chain with knee-forward, hock-back bends, then adding toe sweeps—three forward and one back—radiating from the foot joint with small talon spikes just above the floor. I'm also starting the tail chain, tracing a path backward from the hips.

Then I'm fanning nine long flame-like feather cards from the tail tip, varying their angles horizontally and vertically, with slight downward bend and droop so the tips settle naturally without dipping too low, considering whether to add waviness via sweeps instead of flat cards.

For the feather texture itself, I'm designing an SVG with a cel-shaded flame gradient—hot yellow-white base, orange midsection, crimson tip—built from layered outline shapes rather than smooth gradients, with a serrated, flame-split tip for a more dynamic feather silhouette.

I'm setting up a few palette variants for the feather SVG function, then considering whether to add a subtle glow effect to make the self-lit flame feathers pop on the cards.

Keeping draw call count reasonable per wing row and side, I'll skip tinting and just use distinct texture variants for color variety. For the head, I'm building the skull from a scaled sphere and crafting a hooked beak from swept curves between the head and jaw bones, with gold shading and a separate lower jaw cone for the joint.

For the eyes, I'm placing anime-style decals on the skull surface with a teal-amber iris for contrast against the orange plumage, positioning them symmetrically using mirrored azimuth and elevation offsets around the head's local frame.

For the head crest, I'm arranging flame-card plumes swept back from the crown, orienting the central plume's card plane vertically in the YZ plane for a clean side profile, then spreading the flanking plumes outward with added x-components for a fanned look.

I'll split into two plume sets—central ones with vertical flow, side ones with horizontal flow—and attach them as a head bone. For the chest, I'm scattering small feather-textured flame cards across the body surface with minimum spacing and normal filtering.

I'm giving the chest feathers a gold/orange palette, letting the body cards cover the neck too by extending the body sweep path up through the neck to the head, adjusting the end radius accordingly.

Now I'm defining the skeleton structure: hips as a joint, spine and neck as chains, with the tail as a separate chain branching off the hips with its own tapering radius. I'm working out the coordinates so the spine chain starts at the hips position and ends where the neck chain should begin, keeping each joint's position consistent across the body sweep path and the bone list.

I'm plotting the neck's S-curve rising upward and forward to give the phoenix a proud posture, ending at a head joint, then assembling the full body sweep path with corresponding radii that taper from thick torso to thin neck and head, and figuring out how the hip and tail joints attach as separate chains with their own parent references.

Working out leg geometry next — thigh-to-foot sweep radii tapering down, feathery thigh plumes via cards, then building toes and talons as rods and spikes with specific angled offsets for forward toes and a backward toe, before moving on to define the wing shoulder joint position and its parent attachment to the spine.

For the wings, I'm setting up a chain of named joints per side (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) tagged with a "wing" role, swept with tapering radii and a thick leading-edge covert layer. Now I'm designing a `row` helper to place feather cards along the wing bones, starting with the primaries fanned from wrist to hand with angles rotating from a backward-inner orientation to a forward-outer tip.

Still writing feather placement logic...

Lesser coverts root along the arm line with slight back direction and ember texture. For tip bending, I want the phoenix wing tips to curl upward -- primaries bending +12 toward the flow-up axis while secondaries stay flat, giving that signature upward curl.

Setting up card frames with bone rigging now -- primaries attached to the hand joint, secondaries to wrist, tertials to elbow, lesser coverts to shoulder, so depth ordering follows the skeletal hierarchy. I'm wrapping the wing feather cards in a glow effect, dialing emissive intensity to around 0.75 on the main flight feathers so they read as flame without losing the cel-shaded banding.

Need to check the glow logic only triggers on painted materials and not texture-mapped cards, since cards use separate tint strings rather than flat paint colors. For decorative touches I'm adding a gold filigree collar ring around the neck with a glowing pyro-orange gem, sweeping a thin gold loop around the neck joint where it intersects the body surface, and planning a second ring near the chest.

Finding the chest-front hit point on the body surface to seat an octahedron gem pendant there, glowing orange, bezeled by a gold torus rotated so its axis points outward along the surface normal. I'm also sketching gold tassels hanging from the collar, using upward-facing frames and a reddish-gold tassel texture.

That hanging tassel works fine floating off the chest without touching the ground. Now I'm thinking about adding gold details to the wings and arm, like studded bands or a wrist cuff made from a small ring of frames swept along the arm chain, sized to sit just outside the arm's radius.

I'm skipping extra beak nostril details and small flame puffs at the feet to keep things simple, but I do want flame-like feather plumage scattered across the back of the body, leaning backward for a flowing effect, alongside the other scattered details.

Now I'm writing the SVG texture function for the feathers, defining the viewBox, stroke widths, and curve paths that make up the feather shape...

Still writing feather texture...

I'm assigning textures by row: primaries lean crimson, secondaries blend gold and crimson, tertials stay gold, coverts mix both, with an RNG helper to pick variants per feather for natural variation.

Now I'm setting up vector and frame helpers that take position and direction arrays, then building a fan function to generate rows of feather frames interpolating angle, length, and lift across a wing span.

I'm thinking through how to vary feather lengths across the row without exceeding the mesh part budget—considering whether to batch card calls per feather or use a tapering size function to keep the total mesh count manageable.

Setting up the import list for the plume helper, making sure to only pull in the modules actually used so I avoid unused-import errors, then starting the meta export block for the file.

Naming it "Ember Phoenix" and defining its palette, with countershaded crimson-to-gold cel paints for the body and belly, plus plans for zigzag feather edges.

Shaping the fur/feather edge pattern along the back using a crimson-to-orange gradient with toothed edges and ink outlining, checking that the shadow and axis orientation work properly along the body and neck.

Now defining the head coating with a darker crown gradient, then setting up solid gold trim colors for the beak and claws, plus darker tones for the claws and scaly leg coloring.

Setting up the builder with a root hips joint and a three-point spine chain using catmull curves, then starting the neck chain path with four points.

I'm attaching the head joint to the end of the neck chain, positioning it to align with the neck's terminal point, then adding a jaw joint relative to the head using local offset coordinates for forward and downward placement, with an aim vector pointing further forward and slightly down. Now I'm working out a skull center reference point using similar local offsets from the head joint.

Building the beak geometry...

Jaw sits lower on the head, placed down slightly. Eyes get decal placement with a specific size. Now I'm working out the crest frames, positioning them along the crown and figuring out the direction they should point using the head's orientation axes.

Still defining crest plume positions...

I also want two long trailing head streamers draping down from the back, drooping with a gentle bend, making sure they stay above ground level given the head height. Now I'm moving on to the body sweep shape.

Writing body geometry...

For the body surface, I'm scattering fur/scale cards across it, filtering out the underside, varying card size and lean angle, and cycling through a few texture variants with some randomness. I'm considering adding a slight glow to make the cards pop a bit while still responding to the key light.

Now I'm setting up the wing-arm chains for each side, defining joints for shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand with mirrored positions, then sweeping a tapering radius profile along each arm.

I'm adding gold cuff rings at the wrists, using ring points sampled from the chain and swept with a thin gold tube, checking that the catmull and ring item types line up correctly.

Now I'm placing additional cuffs near the elbow joint, scaling cuff radius based on the arm's local radius there, then sketching a plume function that builds feather frames along a bone with options for bend, flow direction, glow, and lean, matching the Frame and Joint types from the existing module.

Writing row/cards function...

Still tuning primary feather lengths...

Adding secondaries and tertials...

Working through the covert feather layer: I need to place roots along the wing's catmull curve, fanning angles from about 88° near the shoulder down to 60° near the wrist, with lengths shrinking from 0.5 to 0.32 going outward. I'm also figuring out which bone each feather should attach to across shoulder, elbow, and wrist regions so they move naturally with the wing's flex.

Still writing feather placement logic...

Now I'm setting up the leading-edge coverts and small "flame tongue" feathers that stand upright along the wing's top edge, oriented to face outward with a backward flow and a glow effect so they look like flickering flames licking the wing surface. I'm starting to lay out the tail feather anchor positions next.

For the long tail plumes, I'm computing symmetric fan angles and lengths across nine feathers, adjusting their downward bend and vertical drop so the outer feathers curve less than the center ones and all tips stay above zero height. I'm assigning root positions off the tail joint chain and picking a texture set combining an ocellus pattern with two other feather textures.

I'm layering a shorter covert row of seven plumes beneath the main tail, then adding two extra-long outer streamer ribbons with their own bend and width tuned to keep the drop positive. I'm also confirming the sign convention for the curl bend — negative values curl the feather downward away from the flow direction — and working out the sweep setup for the tail base.

Now I'm moving to the legs: placing the hip joint near the body surface, setting a foot target, and computing the limb segment lengths and bend directions for a bird-like bent leg. I'm building the chain structure for each leg, using an array of points as a polyline with named joints (hip, knee, hock, foot) parented to the hips, and checking whether the limb function can accept array-based roots.

Writing leg sweep and feather rings...

Now I'm working out the toe geometry — placing the foot joint tip, computing toe center positions, and building rods with claw spikes at each toe angle, checking that claw tips stay above ground level.

I'm also adding a gold anklet ring around the tarsus at a set point along the leg arc, then moving on to describe the collar loop that wraps around the neck joint using a cutting plane aligned to the bone axis.

For the collar sweep, I'm adding beads distributed along the loop path, each small sphere carrying its own bone weight for glow effects, then positioning a gold chest gem by finding the nearest surface point near the front of the torso around the upper spine.

I'm shaping the gem itself as a small octahedron embedded with a gold torus bezel rotated to align with the surface normal, then anchoring a trio of tassels just below the gem using offset frames for a draped, flowing look.

For the tassel texture, I'm sketching an SVG with a red beaded knot at the top, a gold cap, and a flared tassel body drawn as a tapering path with darker gold strokes for shading detail.

Then I'm figuring out how to scatter cheek tuft cards on the skull sphere, filtering hits to avoid covering the face by checking normal angles, and sizing them small with a leaning flow texture. I'm also planning a sparse scattering of tiny glowing ember octahedra around the wings and tail for extra detail, parented to the nearest bone, and making sure the lowest contact points like toe claws sit right at floor level.

I'm adjusting the toe geometry and claw tip direction so the claw tips land essentially at y=0 for proper floor contact, double-checking tail plumes and wing clearance stay above ground, and confirming the wings keep their spread rest pose with mirrored symmetry. Now I'm adding a back-mounted flame card scatter across the upper body, filtering by upward-facing normals and forward z position, sized larger with a steep lean and texture to resemble rising flames.

Then I'm building a layered SVG function that stacks scaled copies of a feather path with different colors to create a depth effect, anchored at the bottom root point so the texture aligns correctly on feather cards, and adding barb and rachis stroke paths overlaid on top for detail.

Writing feather barb strokes...

I'm defining the ocellus (eyespot) pattern for tail feathers using concentric ellipses in dark red, teal, blue, and cream, then working out the tongue shape path with curves pinching at the tip and base. I'm also setting up tuple typing for card size dimensions and an eye texture helper, then planning a frame type alias and a fan-rendering function before writing out the full code.

Writing feather layout code...

I'll keep embers positioned above the wings to avoid clipping, constraining their x/y/z range accordingly. Then I'm finalizing body paint colors like the beak gradient and claw ink tones, and double-checking imports so I only bring in helpers I actually use—dropping unused ones like countershade.

Now I'm layering furEdge calls for the coat and head, nesting crimson, orange, and gold gradients with zigzag teeth patterns, and setting up the headPaint with its own directional fur texture before moving to leg and limb path details.

Checking types for chains, bones, and joint parameters, then sketching out crest plume definitions with forward/up/left offsets so I can loop through side and center plumes using frames anchored to the head bone.

I'm working out the bend direction for each crest frame by flattening the up vector against the normal, confirming positive bend sweeps the crest backward as intended, then applying similar logic to the side plumes and streamers with their own lengths, widths, and flow directions. Now I'm setting glow strengths and texture variants for the body cards.

Checking the scatter filters and chain naming for wing, tail, and leg placement, then finalizing the toe and foot positions. Writing the file now...
